title: Dexcom G5: Scan Error: Unable to Start scanning (Pixel 4a 5G with Android 12 / S Preview)
body:
**xDrip Nightly build 5th May 2021**
**Dexcom G5 receiver**
**Mobile:** Google Pixel 4a 5G
**Android Version**: S (12 Preview) build bramble-spp3.210325.010-factory-b282d767

**Issue:** Scan Error: Unable to start scanning
**Error log:**
```
Unable to Start Scanning
com.polidea.rxandroidble2.exceptions.BleScanException: Bluetooth Cannot Start (code 0)
No transmitter mac address!
```

Dexcom G5 works perfectly fine with Dexcom Official App and also working fine with MiaoMiao 2 / Bubble 1 & Mini.
With xDrip+ the scanning is not even starting/working.  

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/608650/117578480-6ea1db80-b0e6-11eb-9eec-6921043802c7.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/608650/117578552-d5bf9000-b0e6-11eb-827a-8a5cf80dde0a.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/608650/117580239-00154b80-b0ef-11eb-9169-48306bd62dd5.png)

Looks like either a permission problem or a new security layer. Did xDrip ever ask to bond the transmitter? I assume it is not bonded, yet.

Probably xDrip didn't ask to bond. I used this transmitter with Android 11 and everything was good. After updating, xDrip worked for a while and after some time I got this error. I tried to change a lot of different settings and nothing helps. The last thing I tried is to reinstall the application. After installation of the app, I didn't see a bond request.
@tolot27 Android 12 is now at a beta stage: https://www.google.com/android/beta

I updated to the beta version 
![photo_2021-05-19_23-43-57](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11481452/118888779-61fa6000-b8fc-11eb-9446-e04ee8a50ed2.jpg)

A beta version is still an unreleased version which likely contains bugs. We don't have the time to support unreleased versions. If you believe this problem will persist in the final release and if you like to support us, please try to find out whether the Bluetooth stack has changed fundamentally.

As far as I remember, a new Bluetooth stack named "Gabeldorche" was introduced with Android 11 which can be enabled. Maybe, this stack is now the default stack in Android 12? If yes, please investigate if it can be disabled or if the problem is reproducible in Android 11 if Gabeldorche is enabled.
That's currently the only suggestions I have.

I found this stack in the developer options list and it's disabled by default. I tried to enable it and nothing changed. So probably the reason is different.

I remember a few months ago I have a problem when Android aks to bond every 5 minutes and if I didn't click "bond" I have very similar behavior. How I know, there was some patch to fix this problem. How can I manually bond a transmitter?

I've found the reason. As assumed before, it is a permission problem. A12 introduced two new runtime permissions: [New Bluetooth permissions in Android 12](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/12/features/bluetooth-permissions). As soon as we declare this permissions in the manifest, it should work.
I'll provide a PR soon.
